question: Suppose a ball is placed in front of a concave mirror and a real image that is twice the size of the ball is formed on a screen. The ball and the screen are then moved until the image is five times the size of the object. If the shift of the screen is d, then the shift in the object is:
solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Concave Mirror: A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that converges light to a focal point.
 
• Magnification: The magnification (m) is the ratio of the height of the image (hi) to the height of the object (ho). It is also given by the ratio of the image distance (v) to the object distance (u).
 
• Mirror Formula: The mirror formula relates object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) as:

(1)/(f) = (1)/(u) + (1)/(v)

\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v}

 
• Given that an image is twice the size of the object initially, we can write the initial magnification as:

m₁ = -(v₁)/(u₁) = -2

m_1 = -\frac{v_1}{u_1} = -2

 
• When the image is five times the size of the object, the magnification is:

m₂ = -(v₂)/(u₂) = -5

m_2 = -\frac{v_2}{u_2} = -5

 
• By solving these equations using the mirror formula, we can determine the shifts in the object and screen.

• The magnification produced by a mirror is negative for real images and positive for virtual images.
 
• The sign conventions for concave mirrors are that distances measured in the direction of the incident light are positive, and those measured against the direction of the incident light are negative.
